ACTOR CONFIRMED 2026-09-05 by the owner: RIGGeqD6RqKmlVoQU = valig/linkedin-jobs-scraper, the one already wired. Identity and schema verified against the Apify API, not the store page. CRITICAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED THE SAME DAY: buildInput sent title / rows / publishedAt, but the actor declares keywords / limit / datePosted. Apify IGNORES UNKNOWN INPUT KEYS SILENTLY, so there was no error - the run just used defaults. Consequences: no keyword filter (arbitrary jobs for the location), no recency filter (stale postings), and limit falling back to its default of 100, which made limitPerLocation=30 in config/pipeline.ts completely inert. Eleven locations would have fetched 1,100 jobs a night instead of 330, and the actor bills per result. Six unit tests now assert the field names by name, because a silently-ignored key cannot be caught by a status code. Capabilities newly available and wired: titleInclude/titleExclude post-filters and skipJobId - the last is the only dedupe that SAVES MONEY, since ingest.ts dedupe runs after the results are paid for. VALIDATED by three live Apify runs on 2026-09-17: run ids 7c4f35bd, f3935381 and 683ccbb0, ten results each, $0.005 each. COMPLETED 2026-09-18. Real data through the whole chain: actor input accepted, 10 of 10 records mapped with zero failures, dedupe correctly recognising jobs already held, and skipJobId demonstrated - the run without it fetched ten and discarded all ten as duplicates, the run with it returned genuinely new jobs (Bloomberg, Duffel, Verve, Abtrace, IFS).

SimG is a mandatory, automatic second call after every tailor_cv, isolated so a failed evaluation never costs the CV. It evaluates the CV ONLY - the cover letter is deliberately not revised. prompts/cvg/SIMG.md rewritten from a prose verdict into a priced worklist; config/simg.ts holds the lens weights (ATS .30 / recruiter .35 / HM .35), the pass bar and the composite. Task: [Functional] Capture and measure Apify actor spend alongside AI spend
Description: Record what each Apify run costs and attribute it to the jobs it produced, so total cost per application includes the ingestion cost that surfaced the job, not only the AI cost of scoring it.
Notes: Raised 2026-09-05 on the user's instruction. Apify has a defined cost structure, so this is measurable rather than estimated. DESIGN POINT: ingestion cost is per RUN, AI cost is per APPLICATION - a run cost must be amortised across the jobs it yielded, and a night that surfaces 330 jobs of which 14% qualify makes the per-application ingestion cost roughly 7x the per-job cost. Report both, and never fold the two into one number silently. ingestion_runs already exists (migration 0005) and is the right place to stamp the cost. Depends on the Apify decisions in JSV2S1019. 2026-09-05: THE COST MODEL IS NOW KNOWN AND RECORDED in config/apify.ts, read from the actor API rather than the store page: PAY_PER_EVENT on the Free tier, $0.0004 per dataset item ($0.40/1K results) plus $0.001 per actor start, charged once per GB of memory. estimateFetchCostUsd() prices a plan before it runs. NOTE the start charge means a run that returns NOTHING still costs money, so "fetched and found no new jobs" is not free - the run ledger must record cost even for an empty run. Still to build: stamping actual cost onto ingestion_runs and amortising it across the jobs a run produced. BUILT 2026-09-18. Migration 0011 adds ingestion_runs.cost_usd, applied. STAMPED AT CLOSE, NOT DERIVED - the opposite choice to AI cost, deliberately. AI cost is derived from stored token counts so a rate correction applies to history; Apify publishes price changes and the actor rate WILL move, so re-pricing an old run would quietly rewrite what was actually billed. config/apify.ts carries the date its rates were read; the column carries the money. NULL means free, not zero - a manual upload costs nothing and a stamped zero would claim that had been measured. The ADAPTER reports its own cost rather than the caller computing it, because only the adapter knows its pricing model, and it prices on results RETURNED rather than the limit asked for: limit is a ceiling and charging it would overstate every run. COST PER APPLICATION is the figure that matters and is NOT the per-job cost - a run fetching ten jobs of which one qualifies costs ten results per application, so the per-application figure is roughly ten times per-job. Null while a run has produced no application rather than infinite. scripts/backfill-run-cost.mts priced the three pre-column Apify runs at $0.005 each, defensible only because both inputs are known facts: the result count is stamped and the rate has not moved since it was read.

Task: [Functional] Add a visa-signal pillar to pre-qualification
Description: Add a fifth deterministic filter that looks for a hard visa or sponsorship signal in the job description, so a job with no sponsorship language is screened out before any AI spend, and ScoreG can stop establishing it.
Notes: Raised 2026-09-17 on the owner's instruction. PULLED INTO PHASE 1.5 2026-09-18 at his request. NEEDS A DECISION ON SILENCE BEFORE IT CAN BE BUILT: most London / Amsterdam / Berlin descriptions say nothing about visas at all, so a pillar that screens out everything without sponsorship language would reject nearly the whole intake - the same failure mode as the Axon rejection. The signal must be THREE-STATE: an explicit refusal ("must already have the right to work", "we cannot sponsor") rejects; an explicit offer passes and is recorded; SILENCE PASSES and is recorded as unknown for ScoreG to judge. Only then does it let ScoreG stop establishing sponsorship (JSV2S1149) and pair with the local register (JSV2S1127). DECIDED 2026-09-18 by the owner: the pillar exists to catch EXPLICIT POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE LANGUAGE, not to infer from silence - a clear "no visa sponsorship" callout rejects before any AI spend, and that is the whole point. He will supply a markdown file of the phrasings. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: this is deterministic pattern matching, so it belongs in config/prequalification/ as config - NOT in /prompts, which is prompt text for models (ADR-0002, ADR-0006). 2026-09-19: the owner has the phrasings in a markdown file, to be supplied. DESIGN CONCLUDED 2026-09-19, recorded in the ADR-0006 revision. Three outcomes: REMOVE rejects, KEEP passes, REVIEW passes - and SILENCE IS REVIEW, never REMOVE. Built from the owner's specification file; two headings in it say HARD REMOVE while their bodies say REVIEW (existing-authorisation, permanent/unrestricted) - THE BODIES ARE RIGHT. The UAE need is met by that conservatism rather than by a bypass: existing-authorisation and local-only are already REVIEW, so a UAE exception would only add a hole for Emiratisation. UAE needs a DICTIONARY instead - NOC, transferable visa, spouse visa, must be currently in UAE, UAE Nationals only. Retires mentionsSponsorship() in apify-linkedin.ts in the same change. BUILT 2026-09-19. config/prequalification/visa.ts (rules as data) + features/prequalification/visa.ts (engine). 40 unit tests, including the specification's own §25 cases verbatim. TWO BUGS FOUND BY TESTING MY OWN CODE: the positive patterns matched THROUGH negations and hedges, so "sponsorship is NOT available" registered as an offer and, being an offer beside a refusal, resolved to CONTRADICTORY - the three clearest refusals in the spec were the ones the filter failed to act on. And the proximity rule split on spaces, so "unable," and "sponsorship." were tokens matching nothing, and §17 never fired on any sentence with punctuation. Both fixed; both now have tests. mentionsSponsorship() retired from the actor. NEEDS THE OWNER: confirm the UAE dictionary covers the phrasings he sees.

Task: [Functional] Clear the review and rejected piles into a Bin
Description: Dismiss screened-out jobs individually or in bulk. A soft delete: the job leaves the working queues but keeps its row, verdict and evidence in the database for a future Bin view.
Notes: Raised and BUILT 2026-09-17 on the owner's instruction. Migration 0009 adds raw_jobs.binned_at, applied. Per-row checkboxes plus select-all in one real form, so a single job and a bulk selection use the SAME action - the difference is how many boxes are ticked, not which endpoint is called. SOFT, NOT HARD, for two reasons. The verdict is evidence worth keeping and a rules change may deserve to reconsider it. More practically, a hard delete takes the FINGERPRINT with it, so the same job would be re-ingested and re-presented on the next fetch - the pile would refill itself with exactly what was dismissed. Binned jobs are excluded from listForReview, getFacets, countForReview and countAwaitingReview, and ALSO from requalifyStale: without that, a rules change would re-judge a binned job, promote it to PASS and resurrect something deliberately dismissed. Binning a job that has already become an application is REFUSED rather than skipped silently - it would hide the job while leaving the application pointing at a row the UI treats as deleted. restoreJobs() exists for the future Bin view. Verified against the live database: bin removes it from the rejected list, the row and verdict survive, a promoted job returns 0, and restore puts it back. VALIDATED 2026-09-18 against the live database: binning removed the job from the rejected list while its row and verdict survived with binned_at stamped, binning an already-promoted job returned 0, and restore put it back. The pipeline counts were corrected the same day to exclude binned jobs, so every screen now reconciles.

Task: [Functional] Track per-run outcomes against an ingestion run id
Description: Give every upload and fetch a run id, attribute each ingested job to it, and report what became of that batch: ingested, auto qualified, force qualified, needs review, screened out, moved to Bin.
Notes: Raised and BUILT 2026-09-17 on the owner's instruction. Migration 0010 adds raw_jobs.ingestion_run_id (nullable, ON DELETE SET NULL so losing a run never takes its jobs). MANUAL UPLOADS NOW CREATE A RUN - they previously persisted nothing about themselves, so "which upload brought this job in" had no answer. THE DESIGN POINT IS THE SPLIT between stamped and derived. Stamped on ingestion_runs: fetched, inserted, duplicates, rejected-at-validation - facts about what the run SAW, most concerning rows that never became a raw_jobs record, so if not recorded as they happen they are gone. Derived live: auto qualified, force qualified, needs review, screened out, binned - these describe the CURRENT STATE of jobs that landed, and that state keeps changing long after the run (promoted Tuesday, binned Friday). Stamping them would freeze a number wrong within the hour and force every later action to update a counter on a run it knows nothing about. Auto vs force qualified is whether the GATE said pass or a human overrode it from the review/reject pile. Counting is done in Postgres with `filter (where ...)` in one grouped query - pulling jobs back to count them in JS would move thousands of rows to produce six integers. NOTE: 95 existing jobs predate run tracking and belong to no run. That is surfaced explicitly on the page rather than hidden, because a table whose totals silently disagree with the queue counts is worse than no table. VALIDATED 2026-09-18: four runs recorded with distinct ids, every job in the database attributed to one (0 unattributed), and the funnel reconciles per run. Run attribution now appears on the pipeline table, the review queue and the applications list, and is filterable on both queues as the Fetch facet.

Task: [Functional] Gate-qualified applications are unscored until asked

Notes: Raised 2026-09-19 on the owner's instruction. Precedent is in the skill already: "Source = Recruiter Inbound - skip scoring entirely, auto-classify as PRIORITY" assigns a CATEGORY, never a score.
